findings.title: Reentrancy: external calls before state changes / event emissions in BalancerPoolerV2.unlockCallback
findings.description: unlockCallback performs a sequence of external Balancer Vault calls (swap, settle, sendTo, IERC4626.redeem, addLiquidity) and emits BatchDonated/Pooled events after those calls; donation/pooling state and the waUsdc->usdc conversion happen interleaved with untrusted-vault interaction. Aderyn also flags state-change-after-external-call at BalancerPoolerV2.sol:89 (dispatch path). Callback is reentrancy-guarded only via Balancer's unlock lock; verify no cross-function reentrancy through the minter/hook. Escalate: review whether waUsdc (ERC4626) redeem or vault sendTo can re-enter.

findings.title: State change after external call in NFTMigrator.migrate
findings.description: NFTMigrator.migrate burns V1 tokens and mints V2 tokens across a loop with external calls to v1.burn / v2.mintFor (see SAST-009/010). State mutated after external calls into V1/V2 contracts. Both are owner-deployed trusted contracts, but cross-contract reentrancy through mintFor's downstream dispatch should be confirmed. Escalate to interaction analysis given migrate is user-callable.

findings.title: State change after external call in NFTMinter (V1)
findings.description: V1 NFTMinter mutates state after an external call. V1 is context-only scope; included for completeness. Low priority unless V1 still live.

findings.title: abi.encodePacked with dynamic types feeding a hash in NFTMinterV2
findings.description: abi.encodePacked() used with (potentially) dynamic-length arguments where the packed bytes are hashed (keccak256). If two distinct argument tuples can pack to the same byte string, hash collisions are possible, which can break uniqueness/identity assumptions (e.g. mint keys, dispatcher identifiers). Inspect what is being hashed and whether any argument is attacker-influenced; if dynamic types are present, switch to abi.encode. V1 mirror at NFTMinter.sol:218. Worth escalating to confirm exploitability.

findings.title: abi.encodePacked with dynamic types feeding a hash in NFTMinter (V1)
findings.description: Same pattern as SAST-004 in V1 (context scope). See SAST-004.

findings.title: Unchecked return value of IERC4626(sUSDS).deposit in BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch
findings.description: Return value (shares minted) of IERC4626(_sUSDS).deposit(amount, address(this)) is ignored. The wrapped-share amount is then assumed implicitly. If the ERC4626 wrapper mints fewer shares than expected (rounding, fees, or partial deposit), downstream accounting (donation/pooling amounts) can be wrong. Escalate: this is on the core dispatch (USDS->sUSDS) path introduced by story-025.

findings.title: Unchecked return values of Balancer Vault swap/settle/addLiquidity/unlock in BalancerPoolerV2.unlockCallback
findings.description: Return values of IBalancerVault.swap (line 226), settle (227, 270), addLiquidity (269), and unlock (196) are partially or fully ignored. settle returns credited amount and unlock returns callback bytes; ignoring them can mask under-settlement or partial fills. Tied to SAST-001. Confirm the swap minimum-out and settle credits are validated elsewhere (getIdealBPT/minBPT path).

findings.title: Unchecked Balancer Vault unlock/addLiquidity/settle returns in V1 BalancerPooler
findings.description: V1 BalancerPooler.dispatch ignores IBalancerVault.unlock return (line 54); unlockCallback ignores addLiquidity (87) and settle (88). V1 context scope; same class as SAST-007.

findings.title: Dangerous strict equality (sUSDSAmount == 0) in BalancerPoolerV2.getIdealBPT
findings.description: getIdealBPT() uses a strict == 0 check on sUSDSAmount to branch BPT computation. If this guards the minBPT/slippage computation used by the pooling path, an off-by-dust balance (non-zero but negligible) bypasses the zero-branch and could feed a degenerate ideal-BPT into pooling. Escalate alongside SAST-007 to confirm the minBPT guard is robust (this path is the H-02 slippage fix area, story-026).

findings.title: External calls and require/revert inside the migration loop (DoS / partial migration) in NFTMigrator.migrate
findings.description: migrate() iterates token ids performing external calls per-iteration: IERC1155.balanceOf (66), v1.burn (68), v2.mintFor (71), with a require/revert inside the loop (53) and costly state ops in the loop (43-44). A single failing id (e.g. a token whose mintFor reverts) reverts the whole migration, and an unbounded id range can hit the block gas limit -> migration DoS for users with many/edge tokens. Escalate: assess whether the id set is bounded and whether one bad id can permanently block a user's migration.

findings.title: nonReentrant is not the first modifier (BalancerPoolerV2.pool, BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook)
findings.description: nonReentrant is ordered after other modifiers on BalancerPoolerV2.pool (191) and BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook (hook line 127). Modifiers preceding nonReentrant execute before the reentrancy lock is set; if any of those preceding modifiers make external calls or read mutable state, a reentrancy window exists. Confirm preceding modifiers (pause/auth) are side-effect-free.

findings.title: Privileged setMinter changes the minter without emitting an event
findings.description: ATokenDispatcherV2.setMinter (85) and V1 ATokenDispatcher.setMinter (61) reassign the privileged minter address with no event. Reduces off-chain monitorability of a security-critical role change. QA-grade but the role controls who can drive dispatch; corroborated by Aderyn state-change-without-event.

findings.title: Single-step Ownable across all owner-gated contracts (ownership-transfer footgun)
findings.description: All owner-gated contracts (NFTMinterV2:16, NFTMigrator:12, ATokenDispatcherV2:23, BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook:26, BurnRecorder:11, plus V1 NFTMinter/ATokenDispatcher) use single-step Ownable rather than Ownable2Step; an accidental transfer to a wrong address is irrecoverable. Owner-trust is a documented known issue, so this is QA-level; recorded for the bundle, not for HM escalation.
